finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> does enforce a customer check, which suggests this one was meant to be restricted.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated or authenticated HTTP client supplies inv_id in the URL path.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including its customer field, for any inv_id in INVOICES.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the invoice by the attacker-supplied ID with no comparison to g.user.
The full invoice is returned as JSON.

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, login decorator or g.user comparison exists anywhere in the file. By contrast, get_my_invoice at line 16 compares inv['customer'] to g.user['id']. The repository contains only this one file, so no external middleware is visible. If invoice IDs are unguessable this lowers exploitability, but the endpoint is still unauthorized.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator, before_request hook or g.user comparison and returns jsonify(inv) for any ID, unlike the ownership check at invoices.py:16 in the sibling route (the file is the only one in the repo, so any external middleware is not visible).
